angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 730,485 km at 94.77 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.5518 +/- 0.0135 mas (same row, RUWE 1.15): 94.77 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.05 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Eisner et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4633 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..241E/abstract): 730,485 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.1 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Eisner et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4633 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..241E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5800 +/- 50 K from Eisner et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4633 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..241E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Eisner et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4633 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..241E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4633.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.437, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
